Summary: When Judah faced exile, Isaiah spoke comfort: her warfare is ended, her iniquity pardoned, and her God is coming. Comfort for Judah was never mere sympathy; it was the promise that God had not abandoned His people and would bring them home. That same comfort reaches all who mourn under judgment, pointing to Christ who bears our sorrows.
RelatedEvents: Fall of Jerusalem and the Exile; Cyrus's Decree and Return from Exile
